ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
17. Four charges $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$ and $Q_4$ of same magnitude are fixed along the $x$ axis at $x = -2a$, $-a$, $+a$ and $+2a$, respectively. A positive charge $q$ is placed on the positive $y$ axis at a distance $b > 0$. Four options of the signs of these charges are given in List I. The direction of the forces on the charge $q$ is given in List II. Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists.

List I
P. $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$, $Q_4$ all positive
Q. $Q_1$, $Q_2$ positive; $Q_3$, $Q_4$ negative
R. $Q_1$, $Q_4$ positive; $Q_2$, $Q_3$ negative
S. $Q_1$, $Q_3$ positive; $Q_2$, $Q_4$ negative

List II
1. $+x$
2. $-x$
3. $+y$
4. $-y$

The outer mirror pair Q1 and Q4 is similar: Q1 is positive and repels q toward the upper right; Q4 is negative and attracts q toward the lower right; the vertical components cancel, and the horizontal components both point toward +x. Therefore the total resultant force is along the +x direction.

From the text, Q1 and Q2 are positive, Q3 and Q4 are negative, and q is positive. For the inner pair, positive Q2 repels q along an up-right direction, while negative Q3 attracts q along a down-right direction; because the distances are equal, their vertical components cancel and their horizontal components both point +x. The same argument applies to the outer pair Q1/Q4. Therefore the net force is along +x.

method.method_draft: Compute the signs of the electric-field components at q using Coulomb’s law. From the diagram/text, q is at (0,b), and the four source charges are at x=-2a,-a,+a,+2a. For a charge Qi at xi, the field contribution at q is proportional to Qi(-xi,b)/(xi^2+b^2)^{3/2}. Substitute Q1=Q2=+Q and Q3=Q4=-Q. The y-components from x=-a and x=+a cancel because they have equal denominators and opposite charge signs; likewise the y-components from x=-2a and x=+2a cancel. The x-components are all positive: the positive charges on the left give positive x-components, and the negative charges on the right also give positive x-components. Since q is positive, the force direction is the same as the field direction, namely +x.
